kept.title: Unsafe Dynamic Function Compilation via User-Provided Input
kept.description: The `_compileCreateParamsObject` method in `lib/handler-storage.js` uses `new Function` to construct a function body from user-provided parameter keys. If an attacker can control parameter names (e.g., through specially crafted routing paths), they can escape the function context and execute arbitrary code.
steps_to_exploit: Find a way to inject a string into the route parameter definitions.
Craft a payload that closes the function context (e.g., `'); process.exit(); //`).
Trigger the router registration for this payload.
Observe code execution when the router compiles the parametric handler.
kept.impact: Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the server process.

kept.title: Arbitrary Code Injection in Compiled Router Logic
kept.description: The `_compileGetHandlerMatchingConstraints` method in `lib/handler-storage.js` uses `new Function` to generate runtime logic based on constraint names and derived values. If constraint names can be influenced by input, it allows arbitrary JS injection.
steps_to_exploit: Register a custom constraint strategy with a malicious key name.
Inject a payload into the name of the constraint.
Trigger router lookup to compile the dynamic function.
Observe malicious code execution.
kept.impact: Remote Code Execution (RCE) within the application context.

kept.title: Denial of Service via Regex Redos
kept.description: The router allows users to define custom regex patterns for parameters. If `allowUnsafeRegex` is enabled, the `isRegexSafe` check is skipped, allowing catastrophic backtracking patterns.
steps_to_exploit: Configure the router with `allowUnsafeRegex: true`.
Register a route with a malicious regex (e.g., `/:p((a+)+b)`).
Request a URL path that matches the regex path but triggers exponential backtracking.
Observe the event loop blocking.
kept.impact: Complete service unavailability (Denial of Service) due to CPU exhaustion.

kept.title: Potential Prototype Pollution in Path Sanitization
kept.description: The use of `new NullObject()` and custom object property assignments in `_compileCreateParamsObject` attempts to prevent pollution, but the manual property assignment using template literals might still be susceptible depending on the input.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a parameter name such as `__proto__` or `constructor`.
Observe if the resulting params object maps these sensitive keys.
Use this to influence application logic downstream.
kept.impact: Prototype pollution allowing bypass of security checks or modification of application state.

kept.title: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption in `PrettyPrint`
kept.description: The `prettyPrint` function recursively traverses the entire routing tree. An attacker triggering this functionality (if exposed in an admin endpoint) could exhaust memory by creating deeply nested or extremely broad trees.
steps_to_exploit: Register a massive number of routes or deeply nested parameterized paths.
Call the `prettyPrint` function on the router instance.
Observe memory spike and potential crash.
kept.impact: Memory exhaustion and potential service crash.

kept.title: Missing Authorization for `addConstraintStrategy`
kept.description: The `addConstraintStrategy` method is publicly exposed on the router instance. If this instance is shared or managed, an unauthorized party could register a malicious strategy to intercept traffic.
steps_to_exploit: Gain access to the router instance (e.g., if exported by a plugin).
Call `addConstraintStrategy` with a malicious implementation.
Redirect or log sensitive request data.
kept.impact: Confidentiality and integrity compromise of request routing.

kept.title: Predictable Route Collision Handling
kept.description: The code allows routes to be overwritten or added without strict enforcement of non-collision policies, potentially allowing route hijacking.
steps_to_exploit: Register a route that overlaps with an existing internal or sensitive path.
Observe the order-based resolution overriding the intended handler.
kept.impact: Bypassing intended security handlers by hijacking paths.

kept.title: Insufficient Input Sanitization in Host Constraint
kept.description: The host constraint strategy uses `req.headers.host`, which can be spoofed in many environments. It lacks validation against untrusted input when used to route or categorize requests.
steps_to_exploit: Send a request with a manipulated `Host` header.
Observe the router routing the request to a handler based on the spoofed host.
kept.impact: Information disclosure or bypass of host-based access controls.

kept.title: Insecure `new Function` for prefix matching
kept.description: The `StaticNode` class compiles prefix matching functions dynamically using user-defined prefixes, which could lead to injection if the prefix is not controlled.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a maliciously crafted string as a path prefix.
Trigger the compilation of the match function.
Inject arbitrary code into the logic.

kept.title: Information Disclosure via `prettyPrint`
kept.description: The `prettyPrint` function serializes internal route metadata, including handler function names, which might expose internal class structures or sensitive business logic to an attacker.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an endpoint that calls `router.prettyPrint({ includeMeta: true })`.
Examine the serialized tree to map internal structures.

kept.title: Weak Validation of Constraint Strategies
kept.description: While there is some validation, the strategies themselves are passed as objects that are then executed. A malicious object prototype could be used to cause unexpected behavior.
steps_to_exploit: Create a strategy object with malicious getters or properties.
Pass it to `addConstraintStrategy`.
kept.impact: Unexpected logic execution, potentially leading to privilege escalation.

kept.title: Insecure Default Error Handler
kept.description: The router, by default, might expose implementation details or cause side effects when an error occurs during route matching (e.g., in `_onBadUrl`).
steps_to_exploit: Cause a 404 or bad URL scenario.
Analyze the response for internal path or logic leaks.
kept.impact: Information disclosure of server paths or internal state.

kept.title: Potential Parameter Length Bypass
kept.description: The check `param.length > maxParamLength` occurs after some potential decoding steps, but may be bypassed if complex encoding or unicode normalization is involved.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a URI encoded parameter that expands into a larger string after decoding.
Observe if the length check happens before or after expansion.
kept.impact: Bypass of input validation, potential buffer or state overflow.

kept.title: Dependency Risk: Unsafe Regexp Usage
kept.description: The `safe-regex2` library is used to validate regular expressions. If there is a bypass in this library, it would allow the ReDoS issue (CVE category).
steps_to_exploit: Identify a regex that passes `safe-regex2` but still exhibits catastrophic backtracking.
Register the route and trigger the matching process.

kept.title: Use of `eval`-like behavior in `new Function` for derivations
kept.description: The `Constrainer` builds a custom derivation function using `new Function` with user-supplied header keys, which could be abused if headers are not strictly controlled.
steps_to_exploit: Manipulate headers or context input.
Observe code execution in the `deriveSyncConstraints` path.
